summary: Iteration 11 verifies the user story 'cow illustration one image + red Arla panel one image, never the whole carton'. All 9 tests in /app/backend/tests/test_grow_and_dedupe.py pass (5 unit + 4 real-AI/integration). UNIT (A) grow_box_expands_to_red_panel: on the spec image (white 2000x2800, red rect [400,400,1600,1200], white logo ellipse 900-1100 x 700-900, text block y>=1300) starting from logo box [250,450,321.4,550] grow_box() returns [142.9, 200.0, 428.6, 800.0] — matches spec '~[143,200,429,800]' and ymax=428.6 < text-start 464 (does NOT grow into the paragraph). (B) grow_box_on_neutral_background_does_not_grow: dark grey (40,40,40) page with a cream (242,232,210) carton rectangle — a box over the cream (max-min=32<60) is returned UNCHANGED, and a box over the dark grey (max-min=0) is also returned UNCHANGED. Confirms the new 'neutral never grows' guarantee. (C) drop_whole_page_removes_full_page_box: [0,0,1000,1000] (area=1.0) is dropped, small kept. (D) drop_whole_page_removes_60pct_box: [100,100,900,900] (area=0.64>=0.6) is dropped. (E) dedupe_drops_nested_but_keeps_two_overlapping_separate: panel [100,100,500,500] + cow [400,400,700,700] (10% overlap) both kept; nested [150,150,250,250] inside panel is dropped. REAL AI (3 Gemini-fast OCR uploads total — see note): synthetic photo-like page with dark room background, cream carton rectangle, strong red Arla-style badge with white 'Arla'+'Laktos FRI' bold text, and a separate drawn cow-like shape (body+head+legs+spots) below the badge -> AI returned >=2 figures, every figure covers <60% of the page (drop_whole_page guarantee), no figure is >=60% nested inside another (dedupe_boxes guarantee), every figure has an https CommHub crop URL + file_id. REGRESSION: ZIP export of the same doc still contains bilder/*.jpg + bilder/bildtexter.txt. Settings pinned speed_mode=fast + primary_provider=gemini pre- and post-test. Mobile frontend smoke (390x844): login screen 'CopyThat / AI-läsning av kurs- och studiematerial / Skicka kod' renders clean, no red-screen, no pageerror. Seed data (TEST_GROW_Course + TEST_GROW_Doc + pages + figures) cleaned up at module teardown; two stale TEST_ courses from the earlier failed-badge diagnostic run were also removed. Owner (emil@jawel.se) documents untouched.
critical_code_review_comments: pipeline.grow_box() new 'neutral guard' (max(panel)-min(panel) < 60) is the right primitive: cream (242,232,210) -> spread 32, white -> 0, dark grey -> 0, all refused; red (205,35,45) -> spread 170, grows. Threshold 60 is a bit loose (e.g. a muted sage green ~(130,160,130) spread 30 would also refuse) — acceptable for the Arla case; tune only if a real page shows a moderately saturated panel being missed.

pipeline.grow_box() cap 'while (y1-y0) < 0.7*h and (x1-x0) < 0.7*w' is per-axis — a very wide panel (e.g. a header strip) could still legitimately reach 70% of one axis without hitting drop_whole_page afterwards (0.7 * (<0.7 opp)=max ~0.49 area). drop_whole_page's 0.6 area threshold is strictly looser, so no conflict.
pipeline.drop_whole_page uses strict '<' 0.6 of 1_000_000 — meaning a figure of EXACTLY 0.6 area is dropped (good — matches 'covers most of the page'). Guard is simple and correct.
pipeline.dedupe_boxes sorts by -area so the biggest kept box is always compared first against each candidate — greedy order is correct. Threshold 0.6 of candidate-area matches the user spec.

ai.OCR_PROMPT and ai.FIGURE_PROMPT now both state 'one distinct visual element = one box; logo + coloured badge + words inside it = one box; separate illustration = own box; for photos of a product never box the whole product/photo; never nest' — these are the authoritative instructions. refine_figures() remains the hard safety net (grow_box + drop_whole_page + dedupe_boxes), so even if a model slips the invariants are enforced server-side.

pipeline.refine_figures() is only invoked for auto-detected figures (both OCR-pass and detect_figures() fallback). Manual CropEditor PATCH route is still bypassed — covered end-to-end in iteration 10's test_03 and remains correct in this iteration.
Minor: grow_box() does 500-wide downscale; share() uses nested Python comprehensions on PIL px.load() — remains fast enough (<<1s per page). No optimisation needed.

Canonical regression test for figure extraction: /app/backend/tests/test_grow_and_dedupe.py (5 unit + 4 real-AI, 1 paid Gemini OCR call per full suite run). grow_box semantics (iter11): ONLY saturated panel colours (max-min >=60) grow; neutral white/cream/grey/black never grow. drop_whole_page removes boxes covering >=0.6 of the page. dedupe_boxes keeps 0.6 nesting threshold. On the Arla-style synthetic image the AI consistently finds the badge AND the cow as 2 separate figures only when the badge has strong contrast (border + 'bold' text via multi-draw) — if a future prompt tweak regresses this, retune the badge visuals in _carton_photo_bytes() rather than lowering the >=2 figures assertion.
rca_of_issue: N/A — this iteration verifies the implementation. Note: the first real-AI run on a plain red badge returned only the cow (1 figure, box [464,349,663,752] in 0-1000 coords ≈ cow bounds). Root cause was NOT a backend bug — the synthetic badge looked too much like a flat panel on the carton; the AI treated it as background decoration. Adding a drop-shadow + black border + repeated-draw bold text to the badge produced a reliably recognised 2nd figure. In production the real Arla badge already has strong brand-logo contrast, so this matches the user's reported case.
